title: Permutationally Invariant Quantum State Tomography for Fermions
abstract: Quantum state tomography provides complete information about a quantum state, but its measurement cost generally grows exponentially with system size. In many-particle quantum simulators, this challenge is further compounded by the limited accessibility of local measurements and controls. Here we develop a tomography protocol for permutation-invariant fermionic many-body states with U(1) particle-number symmetry. We show that any such state is completely determined by the distribution of the total particle number and the occupation of a single collective mode within each particle-number sector, both of which are accessible in current ultracold-atom experiments. The number of required observables scales only linearly with the system size. More generally, the protocol reconstructs the permutation-symmetrized component of arbitrary U(1)-symmetric fermionic states, which can still encode nontrivial many-body and state-level structure beyond conventional few-body observables. We demonstrate this protocol in interacting non-Gaussian states of the complex Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and in free-fermion chains across a Lifshitz transition. This framework opens a route toward information-theoretic characterization of strongly correlated itinerant quantum matter in experimentally realistic fermionic quantum simulators.
summary: The paper introduces a scalable tomography protocol for fermionic many-body states by exploiting particle permutation symmetry. It shows that the full state information can be captured using only the total particle number distribution and the occupation of one collective mode, both measurable in cold atom setups. This opens a pathway to characterize strongly correlated quantum matter experimentally.
main_problem: To develop a scalable quantum state tomography protocol for fermionic many-body states that avoids the exponential measurement cost associated with full reconstruction.
main_result:
The permutation-symmetrized density matrix can be fully reconstructed using only two quantities—the total particle number distribution ($p_q$) and the conditional occupation of a single collective mode ($
u_q$)—which scale linearly with system size.
method: The protocol leverages $U(1)$ particle-number symmetry to decompose the state and utilizes properties derived from permutation invariance (Schur's Lemma) to simplify the required observables.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to fermionic many-body states, particularly those with $U(1)$ particle-number symmetry, demonstrated using models like the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and free-fermion chains in optical lattices.
key_observables:
Total particle-number distribution ($p_q$) and conditional occupation of a uniform mode ($
u_q$).
important_parameters: System size ($N$), temperature/inverse coupling strength ($ eta$), and the filling parameter ($\varrho$).
main_assumptions: The protocol is restricted to states with $U(1)$ particle-number symmetry, and some derivations rely on asymptotic approximations (e.g., Stirling's formula).
figures_summary:
Figure 1 shows reconstruction using the SYK model via estimated $
u_q$ and $p_q$. Figure 2 demonstrates calculating von Neumann entropy for free fermions across a Lifshitz transition, showing predicted nonanalyticity.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the scalability problem of tomography, derives the PIQT protocol based on symmetry constraints, applies it to reconstruct complex states (SYK), and then uses the framework to calculate thermodynamic quantities like von Neumann entropy for free fermions near a critical point.
why_interesting:
This work provides an information-theoretic characterization tool that translates difficult quantum state reconstruction problems into measurable observables ($p_q, 
u_q$) directly accessible in modern ultracold atom experiments.
